outcome.technical: Deleted _closed_part and _CLOSERS from plugins/audit/hooks/_config.py. runnable_text is the raw join again, via the new runnable_parts(cmd, pipe_data) ([text] + shell + code). New part_ends_open(part) runs the same comment-aware _context_step walk and reports an open quote, an open substitution or a pending escape. It never appends anything. New runnable_clauses(cmd, pipe_data) splits each part with command_clauses on its own, so an open part becomes one clause for its reader's strict reading. Docstring: the claim that a closer seals only text its shell never runs is replaced by the rule (raw join; ask each part; never close one by hand; why a closer is wrong). Adjacent files I had to edit, all allowed by the plan gate: plugins/audit/hooks/guard-history-rewrite.py, where git_calls returns None (the text reading) unless parts_read_alone(command), meaning every part ends closed in _config's quoting AND tokenizes under the guard's own _shell_pieces, and _shell_moves now uses runnable_clauses; .claude/hooks/guard-release.py, where _publishers and _shell_moves use runnable_clauses instead of command_clauses(runnable_text(...)). guard-uncommitted reaches the fix through parser().git_invocations, so the only change there is to its selftest. guard-secrets-read.py was NOT changed. Every rule reading _shell_text, _executed_text or runnable's read arms is a re.search over the view or a per-clause regex word scan (_extra_read_hit), and the inline-eval arm already grades each body as its own clause, so no quote state crosses a part there. s79-s83 block.
